directiveSource: Explicit user instruction: adopt selective baseline-first process for all remaining cities
strategy: Breadth-first culturally significant experiences, then optional historical gap audits; stop exhaustive neighborhood-by-neighborhood searches.
scope: All remaining and revisited cities, not just Boston; restaurants, bars, pubs, theater, opera, music, museums, notable attractions and exceptional experiences.

include: Michelin stars/Bib Gourmand/Green Star and historically relevant Michelin selections
James Beard winners, finalists, notable semifinalists, distinguished chefs/bars
CAMRA recognized pubs and major brewing competition wins
Major arts and performance institutions, significant performances, culturally defining historic venues
Historically iconic or locally significant experiences
Notable hospitality/design awards, landmark cocktail bars, destination restaurants
Local reader recommendations and ordinary neighborhood taprooms only when exceptionally distinctive or needed to jog a known memory

interview.stopRule: Mark baseline complete after high-value candidates and one targeted historical-miss pass; do not demand exhaustive neighborhood coverage.

recordsPolicy.confirmedVisit: Create public visitor candidate regardless of awards; publication subject to separate explicit story review.
recordsPolicy.uncertainVisit: Private, not confirmed, never automatically published.
recordsPolicy.futureWishlist: Private and explicitly not visited; never public.
recordsPolicy.closedVenueInterest: Private historical interest only, not actionable future wishlist.
recordsPolicy.awards: Attribution must distinguish specific venue, chef, brewery brand, beer product, editorial list, community ratings, formal medals, and historical context.
